relevance_note: A review of primary immunodeficiencies that describes one identifiable person with a TNFAIP3 variant: "By using WES in an infant with lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly and persistent fever, Takagi et al.^37 found a biallelic mutation in the TNFAIP3 (HA20) gene, predicting a truncated protein."
method_note: Read the whole paper (the file has no 'Supplementary material' section); the only TNFAIP3 (A20) content is one paragraph under 'Recently reported primary immunodeficiencies' and the TNFAIP3 row of Table 5, both transcribed by hand (no script). In-scope people: only the infant of Takagi et al.^37, because the review gives individual-level facts about this person ('an infant with lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly and persistent fever' and a 'biallelic mutation in the TNFAIP3 (HA20) gene'); label taken by rule 4 ('ref [37] patient'), is_proband false (a review, the person is never called a proband; the span given for is_proband is the sentence describing this person, which contains no proband wording). No rows for: the Zhou et al.^36 families ('found in six unrelated families who mostly presented with childhood-onset systemic inflammation'), the cohort studies ^38,39 ('Behcet disease, Crohn's disease, periodic fever with aphthous pharyngitis and adenitis (PFAPA), polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis') and the gene-level Table 5 row - none gives individual-level detail. cohort_size_as_stated is null: the review has no cohort of its own, and the counts it mentions (six families, other studies' cohorts) belong to other papers. The TNFAIP3 variant is tied to this person but no variant description is printed (only 'a biallelic mutation ... predicting a truncated protein'), so variant_original_string is 'not reported' (v3 rule). 'biallelic' is not an allowed zygosity value and no variant class is stated (a truncated protein is not called frameshift or nonsense), so zygosity and variant_type_as_stated are 'not reported'. Contradiction noted: the same review says TNFAIP3 (HA20) defects are 'heterozygous LOF mutations' with 'Autosomal Dominant' inheritance (Table 5), which conflicts with this person's 'biallelic' mutation; since those statements are about the gene and other cohorts, zygosity and inheritance stay 'not reported'. functional_evidence_statement keeps two spans: the first is about this person's cells ('patient-derived T cells'), the second about cells transfected with the mutant studied for this patient; a stricter reading would keep only the first. Phenotypic feature 'persistent fever' is recorded as stated, but the checklist item 'recurrent fever' stays 'not reported' because the paper says persistent, not recurrent. The paper says only 'an infant' and gives no sex, so sex and all age fields are 'not reported'. No stacked cells (' / ') and no absent/negative table symbols occur for any person in this paper.
